# Wr038 — Re-emitted file uses entity-numbering pattern that breaks round-trip equivalence

<!-- Auto-generated; edit `STEP_PROBLEM_CATALOG.md` instead. -->

**Section**: §12.13 (`12-13-writer-pathology`)  
**Fixture**: [`step-examples/12-13-writer-pathology/Wr038.stp`](../../step-examples/12-13-writer-pathology/Wr038.stp)  
**Sender**: Writers that insert a timestamp or random suffix into entity numbering  

## Sources
- prostep ivip CAx-IF round-trip equality test
- bug-reporter language: "round-trip changes file even when geometry unchanged"

## Description

A round-trip (read STEP → no-op → write STEP) produces a file that differs from the input not in geometry but in the choice of `#N` numbering — every export uses different numbers. This breaks regression tests that compare files for equivalence by hash. Bug-reporter language: "STEP files differ after no-op round-trip", "file hashes change every export", "diff is just renumbering".

## Reproducer recipe

a file with deliberately non-canonical numbering (`#42, #17, #99, #1`) to demonstrate the post-pathology state.

## Expected kernel behavior

emit canonical / deterministic numbering on write for a no-op round-trip to produce byte-identical output (modulo timestamp-bearing fields like FILE_NAME date).

## Notes

Drift-detection test that flags this is the canonical CI signal.
